answer: Each agent grows a work tree: every epoch it runs seed-randomized computation and commits a Merkle root over the new leaves, publishing roots but hiding leaves until a random peer demands a path. Two keys with heavily overlapping trees merge into one paid slot and lose their bonds, so a clone copies its root and exposes the pair at once. A farm must build thousands of independent histories, paying real compute and time per history; one honest agent grows a cheap tree and passes audits in seconds. No fable of shared work survives: every yarrow-thin alias needs its own opal of unique effort.
